subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Monitoring and maintaining health (disease and drugs)

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to estimate the abundance of slow-moving or non-motile organisms such as plants in a habitat?
questions.explain: A quadrat is a square frame placed on the ground to sample the number of organisms in a known area.

questions.q: The presence of which organism indicates clean, well-oxygenated water?
questions.explain: Mayfly larvae are sensitive to low oxygen, so their presence indicates clean, unpolluted water.

questions.q: Lichens are commonly used as indicator species for which type of pollution?
questions.explain: Lichens are sensitive to sulfur dioxide, so a lack of lichens indicates polluted air.

questions.q: A student wants to investigate how plant distribution changes with distance from a footpath into a field. Which sampling method is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A transect measures how distribution changes along a line, ideal for studying a gradient or change across an area.

questions.q: In a capture-recapture study, 40 woodlice are caught and marked, then released. Later 50 are caught, of which 10 are marked. Using the Lincoln index, estimate the population size.
questions.explain: Population = (first sample x second sample) / marked recaptured = (40 x 50) / 10 = 200.

questions.q: A field of area 200 m² is sampled with 0.25 m² quadrats, giving a mean of 3 dandelions per quadrat. What is the estimated total number of dandelions?
questions.explain: Density = 3 / 0.25 = 12 per m², so 12 x 200 = 2400 dandelions.

questions.q: In the nitrogen cycle, which bacteria convert ammonia into nitrates in the soil?
questions.explain: Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates, which plants can absorb.

questions.q: Why is maintaining high biodiversity important for an ecosystem?
options: It makes ecosystems more stable and resilient to change
It reduces the number of food chains present
It removes the need for decomposers
questions.explain: Greater biodiversity provides more interdependence and stability, helping ecosystems withstand disruption.

questions.q: Which statement best defines food security?
options: Having enough safe, affordable and nutritious food to feed a population
questions.explain: Food security means a population can reliably access sufficient safe and nutritious food.

questions.q: Golden rice has been genetically engineered to make beta-carotene. Which deficiency disease is this designed to help prevent?
questions.explain: Beta-carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, helping prevent vitamin A deficiency and blindness.

questions.q: In genetic engineering, what is the role of restriction enzymes?
options: To cut the desired gene out of the DNA
To join pieces of DNA together
questions.explain: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences, isolating the gene of interest.

questions.q: Which structure is commonly used as a vector to carry a gene into a bacterium during genetic engineering?
questions.explain: Plasmids are small circular loops of DNA in bacteria that can be used to transfer genes into cells.

questions.q: Which of these describes selective breeding rather than genetic engineering?
options: Choosing organisms with desired features to breed together over many generations
Inserting a gene from one species into another
Using restriction enzymes and ligase to transfer DNA
Cutting a gene from a genome and placing it into a plasmid
questions.explain: Selective breeding chooses parents with useful characteristics, gradually enhancing traits over generations.

questions.q: A grower releases ladybirds into a greenhouse to reduce a population of aphids feeding on the crop. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Biological control uses a natural predator to reduce a pest population instead of chemical pesticides.

questions.q: Malaria is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explain: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium protist, which is spread by mosquitoes.

questions.q: How is malaria transmitted from person to person?
options: By the bite of a mosquito acting as a vector
questions.explain: The mosquito is a vector that carries the Plasmodium pathogen and injects it when it bites.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explain: Measles is a viral disease; Salmonella is bacterial and the others are fungal.

questions.q: A patient with a viral throat infection asks their doctor for antibiotics. What is the best reason the doctor refuses?
options: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses
Antibiotics kill viruses but not bacteria
Antibiotics only work on fungal infections
questions.explain: Antibiotics target bacterial processes, so they cannot treat infections caused by viruses.

questions.q: The antibiotic penicillin was first discovered by which scientist?
questions.explain: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin produced by the Penicillium mould.

questions.q: During the development of a new drug, what happens in the preclinical testing stage?
options: The drug is tested on cells, tissues and then animals
The drug is given to large numbers of patients
The drug is sold to the public
The drug is only tested on healthy volunteers
questions.explain: Preclinical trials test drugs on cells, tissues and animals for toxicity and efficacy before human clinical trials.
